entity_title: Work permit doubles as residence permit
fact_text: A work permit issued by the Ministry of Labour and Social Security also functions as the holder's residence permit for its full validity, so a separately issued residence permit is not required while the work permit is valid.
evidence_quote: The work permit is replaced as a residence permit, so residence permission is not necessary as long as it lasts.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a foreign worker needs both a work permit and a separate residence permit. Actually the valid work permit itself serves as the residence permit (LFIP No. 6458 Art. 27). Action: do not file a separate residence-permit application while the work permit is valid.

entity_title: Register at migration directorate within 20 working days
fact_text: A foreigner who has received a work permit must register with the Provincial Directorate of Migration Management within 20 working days of entering Türkiye.
evidence_quote: Foreigners who have received the work permit must register to the Provincial Directorate of Migration Management within 20 working days from the entry date to our country.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the work permit alone completes all arrival formalities. Actually the holder must still register in person with the Provincial Directorate of Migration Management within 20 working days of entry. Action: book the migration-directorate registration immediately after arrival.

entity_title: Work visa from a Turkish mission before entry
fact_text: Work permit applications normally begin with the foreigner applying for a work permit and work visa at a Turkish foreign representative office (consulate) abroad; an in-country ('domestic') application is only possible for foreigners already holding a residence permit valid for at least six months.
evidence_quote: Work permit applications generally start with foreigners applying for a work permit and visa to the relevant foreign representative offices of the Republic of Türkiye.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you can fly to Türkiye and sort out the work permit locally. Actually the standard route requires applying for the work visa at a Turkish consulate in your country of nationality first. Action: start the consulate work-visa application before travelling unless you already hold a 6-month+ residence permit.

fact_text: A foreigner in Türkiye is assigned a T.C. Foreigner Identity Number that starts with 99, used for the domestic work-permit application and other official transactions.
evidence_quote: the foreigner has a T.C. Foreigner Identity Number starting with 99.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed only Turkish citizens have a national ID number. Actually registered foreigners receive a T.C. Foreigner Identity Number beginning with 99, required for domestic work-permit filings and everyday admin. Action: obtain and record the 99-prefixed foreigner ID number for all official processes.

entity_title: Permit is tied to one employer
fact_text: A Turkish work permit is tied to a specific employer; an application to work for a different employer is treated as a first (new) application rather than an extension.
evidence_quote: applications to work for a different employer are considered within the scope of the first application.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a work permit lets you change jobs freely like a general visa. Actually it is bound to the sponsoring employer, and moving to a new employer restarts the process as a first application (losing extension continuity). Action: plan any employer change as a fresh permit application.

entity_title: First work permit lasts up to one year
fact_text: On a first (definite) work permit application the foreigner is granted a permit valid for up to one year, tied to a specific workplace and job; longer durations come only through subsequent extensions (up to two, then three years).
evidence_quote: the foreigner is granted a work permit valid for up to one year at the first application

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed an assignment permit is granted for the full multi-year posting up front. Actually the first work permit is capped at one year; extensions later reach up to two then three years. Action: budget for a renewal within the first year of the assignment.

entity_title: Turquoise Card has a 3-year transition period
fact_text: The Turquoise Card for highly qualified foreigners is first granted with a provisional three-year transition period; it becomes indefinite only after the holder applies (within 180 days before the period ends) to remove the transition annotation.
evidence_quote: Turquoise Card is granted with a provisional period of first three years as a transition period.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the Turquoise Card grants indefinite work-and-residence rights immediately. Actually it starts as a three-year transition period and becomes indefinite only after a timely application to lift the transition. Action: diarise the transition-removal application (within 180 days before the 3-year mark).

fact_text: For a foreign employee the notification to the Social Security Institution (SGK) is deemed timely if made within 30 days from the start date of the permit stated on the work permit document.
evidence_quote: notifications made to the Social Security Institution within 30 days from the start date of the permit in the work permit document

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the work permit automatically enrols the worker in social security. Actually a separate SGK notification is required and is timely only within 30 days of the permit start date. Action: ensure the employer files the SGK insured-entry notification within 30 days of the work permit start date.

fact_text: For Turkish income tax, a person who resides in Türkiye for a continuous period of more than six months within one calendar year is not a non-resident taxpayer and is instead treated as a resident (full-liability) taxpayer.
evidence_quote: who do not reside in Türkiye for a continuous period of more than six months within one calendar year.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a relocating employee stays taxable only in their home country. Actually residing in Türkiye for a continuous period of more than six months in a calendar year makes you a resident (full-liability) taxpayer. Action: assess Turkish tax residency and the applicable double-tax treaty before the six-month point.

fact_text: A work permit extension must be applied for before the permit expires, and the application can be made starting from 60 days before the existing permit's expiry date.
evidence_quote: an application must be made before the expiration of the permit, starting from 60 days before the expiration of the existing work permit.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a work permit can be renewed any time around its expiry. Actually the extension window opens 60 days before expiry and must be filed before the permit lapses; a late filing is evaluated as a first application. Action: file the extension within the 60-day pre-expiry window.

entity_title: 10-day grace to switch to a residence permit
fact_text: When a work permit expires, the holder has 10 more legal days (as with a residence permit) during which a suitable residence permit can be applied for.
evidence_quote: when the work permit expires, you have 10 more legal days, as in the residence permit and you can apply for a suitable residence permit during this period.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed a person falls out of legal status the instant a work permit lapses. Actually there is a 10-day legal grace period after expiry to apply for a suitable residence permit. Action: if the work permit ends without renewal, apply for a residence permit within 10 days.
